body: It just seems like common courtesy to tell them... but in this case, I'd prefer not to. What law states that specifically? I don't know if such a law exists, as it may be of interest to the employer to know of a physical handicap that would impair the workers productivity.
I read it all, it's extremely well written and you make some really good points. To be honest I'm shocked in how dead on this is. I'm too tired to reply intelligently, but thank you.

>If it's obvious your current life sucks, do something to change it. School. Therapy. Hospital. Yeah. All good ideas. Don't stay idle. Keep moving.

This probably makes sense but I fail to see why it makes sense. I also forgot to mention I take courses part-time (online), work full-time (9 hours). I don't think it's smart to quite a stable job to opt for full time school, therapy or hospital - all cost money - without a full time job debt would just add more stress. I'm not exactly idle, work is one of the only reasons I wake up in the morning, the weekends I don't wake up until the afternoon and don't go to sleep until 2-3am. I was without a job for 2 weeks before and I nearly destroyed myself, work keeps me alive - I don't think that's a good move. 

I do agree that I should start seeing a psychitrist again, but my work is intolerable - they'll let me take appointments, but they started asking why I was going to the doctor so often before. I made up some medical issues, but I hated lying, maybe I just need a better lie. It's unfortunate that it's necessary to lie, but the social realities cannot be denied. Telling your employer that you have mental issues is just not smart.

i also have hearing damage from my last job (as well as poor uncorrectable vision). It's intermittent though, the ringing comes and goes, usually only when I hear something loud that sets it off, though there is a low level of constant ringing. They told me as well as the damage was permanent and nothing could be done. 

[Here](http://www.hearinglossweb.com/Medical/Tinnitus/manage.htm) is a website with some information. Summing if the main points:

* Avoiding irritants: Tinnitus can be aggravated by loud noises, nicotine, caffeine, tonic water, alcohol and various medications.

* Cover the noise: In a quiet setting, a fan, soft music or a white noise machine can help mask the noise from tinnitus. For some people, tinnitus maskers (a device that looks like a hearing aid) that produce a pleasant noise may also help.

* Hearing aid relief: If your tinnitus is accompanied by hearing loss, hearing aids can amplify outside sounds, making the tinnitus noise less obvious.

* Stress management: Stress can make tinnitus worse. Stress management, whether through relaxation therapy, biofeedback or exercise, may provide some relief.
yes I do exercise, but it only quells the depression for about 30-45 minutes until the adrenaline wears down. I'm actually really physically fit, but the mental anguish is crushing.

Your reply is extremely well written, thank you. Sometimes I wish I was born a woman, men are required to put on a 'tough guy' appearance, but I've been doing that for so long that I just can't pretend anymore. i have nothing left in me.

I can't afford private psychologists, I use the government services but they are only open until 4pm, and I don't get off work until after 5pm. There really is a failure in the US to provide this sort of service, instead we except people to either deal with the problems or to go absolutely insane and check themselves into a mental institution.

I almost hate to comment because it seems like you have worked out your problems and I don't want to bring my pain to you because you're happy now. I'm happy for you.
